description.value: An fMRI study examined visual processing of sexual penetration and disgust-related stimuli in women with primary vaginismus, dyspareunia, and sexually asymptomatic controls.

value: the overlap in brain areas activated in response to sexual penetration and disgust would be especially pronounced in those who have a problem with sexual penetration (e.g., vaginismus).

value: The PEN>BOD contrast revealed widespread bilateral occipitotemporal and occipitoparietal activity, including the superior parietal lobule, bilateral ventral premotor cortex, posterior thalamus, dorsal midbrain, hypothalamus, and basal forebrain. Brain responses to PEN did not differ significantly between groups.

spans.text: Over subjects and groups significant (p<.05, FWE corrected) activity was found in widespread, bilateral occipitotemporal and occipitoparietal areas, the latter reaching up to include the superior parietal lobule ( Figure 1 ). More rostral in the brain, activity was found in bilateral precentral gyrus corresponding to ventral premotor cortex. Substantial subcortical activity was found, centered posteriorly on the pulvinar of the thalamus and the dorsal midbrain, and anteriorly on the hypothalamus and basal forebrain ( Table 2 ).

value: There was extensive overlap between brain responses to PEN and disgust stimuli, with more shared activity for animal-reminder disgust than for core disgust. This overlap involved occipitotemporal and parietal regions, inferior frontal gyrus, and ventral midbrain, and did not differ between groups.

spans.text: The overlap between PEN- and disgust-induced brain activation was extensive with more overlap i.e., more shared voxels, observed between PEN and A-R disgust than between PEN and core disgust activation maps, across the three groups.
